gaps.sentence: I want you ___ the truth, whatever it is.
gaps.explanation: want + object + to-infinitive: want you to tell.
too + adjective + to-infinitive: too young to stay.

gaps.sentence: If you keep ___ like this, you'll exhaust yourself.
gaps.explanation: keep (+ on) is followed by -ing: keep working.

gaps.sentence: We stopped ___ something to eat at the motorway services.
gaps.explanation: 'Stopped to get' = paused for the purpose; 'stopped getting' would mean quit eating.
fail takes the to-infinitive: failed to meet.
Negative infinitive: promised not to be late — 'not' goes before 'to'.

gaps.sentence: They agreed ___ the deadline by a week.
gaps.explanation: 'Agree to do something' takes the to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: She was on the verge of ___ up her job to sail around the world.
gaps.explanation: 'On the verge of' ends in a preposition, so the gerund follows.
